Mayor Valencia called the special meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California and via videoconference pursuant to
Assembly Bill 361. City Council was present in its entirety with Councilmembers Ayala,
Perez, and Ramirez, Vice Mayor Rios, and Mayor Valencia responding to roll call. Also
present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, Theresa Devoy, City Clerk, and
Department Directors.

REPORTS

FISCAL YEAR 2023/24 PROPOSED BUDGET

Jana Stuard, Director of Finance/Treasurer, gave a presentation regarding the proposed
balanced Fiscal Year 2023/24 budget sharing that the total proposed budget of $261
million, which is an increase of 25% from last fiscal year. It is comprised of $71 million
from General funds and the remaining balance is from Enterprise, Capital Reserves,
grants, and restricted funds. Enhancements will be primarily in Public Safety under the
Sheriff’s contract. Contribution rate to the Public Employees Retirement System is
39.33% of full-time salaries; up 1.3% from last fiscal year. The General Fund represents
34% of the entire budget. There is $14.1 million from the capital reserve funds designated
for various capital improvement projects. Ms. Stuard reported that overall, the combined
ending capital reserves are estimated at $30.1 million. In reference to General Fund
revenues, the budget includes an expected decrease in Sales Tax and increases in
Property Taxes, Utility User Tax, and Franchise Fees. Ms. Stuard also reported that total
proposed revenues are budgeted at $74.6 million, with an overall 4% or $2.7 million
increase. The General fund unassigned budgetary fund balance is projected at $15.1
million as of June 30, 2024.

Following the presentation, City Council discussion ensued seeking information regarding
the Children’s Dental program; the Barn Design Concept; plans to address the decreased
parking structure revenue; how Measure P is being allocated, and what is being proposed
for additional Public Safety expenditures; the increase of an additional Net Team through
the Sheriff’s Department using Measure P funds; leasing impacts on the new planned
residential/retail project at City Hall; Youth and Family Intervention/Community Worker;
adding a 5K Walk/Run; and bus stop improvements. City Council thanked staff for their
work on the budget.

Mr. Gomez provided responses indicating that there may be another Care Court coming
into the Norwalk Superior Courthouse in December and staff is looking at the possibility
of leasing a floor; any leases would take into consideration possible conflicts; funding
has been increased by $4 million for the Sheriff’s contract and an additional Deputy is

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT FOR PREPARATION OF A COMPREHENSIVE FEE STUDY AND

Background:

A Comprehensive Fee Study is generally completed once every 10 years with the purpose of
establishing fees, rates, and charges for services, provided that such fees, rates, and charges
do not exceed the estimated reasonable cost of providing said services.

To reflect total program costs, a Cost Allocation Plan is also necessary to allocate general City
administrative costs to all City programs. It is both common practice and advantageous to the
City to complete both the study and plan concurrently.

The results of these studies provide the City with the knowledge and tools to ensure that current
cost recovery practices are compliant with local and state laws while developing cost recovery
policies that balance the needs of the General Fund against subsidies to promote growth and
development. This will allow the City Council to update the City’s fees to reflect current costs, or
to subsidize a portion of fees for specific activities at the City Council’s discretion.

The City’s last User Fee Study was completed in May of 2007. In an effort to accurately, fairly,
and reasonably determine the full cost of providing services to the community, an updated fee
study and accompanying cost allocation plan is needed.

On April 3, 2023 the City issued a Request for Proposal (“RFP”) 23-721 to solicit firms to prepare
the Comprehensive User Fee Study and Cost Allocation plan. Requested services included:
  • Comprehensive review of the City’s existing fee structure.
  • Comparing service costs with existing recovery levels.
  • Surveying comparable cities in California to determine best practices and trends.

projects (CIP) which are currently in progress. The CIPs require California Environmental Quality

projects also require review of proposed design typically off-site and anything that provides
services to the project site. There are presently ongoing projects and programs, which require
traffic engineering and oversight. These include traffic signal improvements projects; ongoing
management of the City adopted speed hump program; the on-going citywide multi-faceted
traffic and related requests; all of which require review, analysis and technical responses. This

Background:

Bellflower, Cerritos, Downey, Hawaiian Gardens, Lakewood and Norwalk. The WDB is similar
to a career center, offering job search assistance, vocational training and career counseling and
assessment. Additionally, the WDB has a number of services for business. These include
employee and potential employee assessment services, training programs, and a pool of
potential employees. The WDB partners with businesses, schools, and government entities to
coordinate resources and services.

Candidates to serve as representatives are nominated by a Norwalk business association (such
as the Chamber of Commerce, Kiwanis, Optimists, etc.) to serve two-year terms. The City
Council then either accepts or denies the nomination. If accepted by the City Council, the
nominee is submitted to the WDB Policy Board, where it will be upheld or rejected.

Representation

The City has two seats on the WDB that typically serve two-year terms. If the two-year term
expires and the representatives have not yet been re-appointed, they continue to serve until
either re-appointed or replaced by the Policy Board.

Mr. Tracy Polley has represented the City since November 2014 and is in good standing with
the WDB. Mr. Derthick represented the City since 2010, but resigned from the WDB leaving a

Background:

charges to pay for the operation and maintenance of the City’s sewer system, including capital
replacement costs. Ordinance No. 13-1642 provided that beginning July 1, 2014, the sewer
service charge could be increased annually through July 1, 2018 by an amount equal to the
annual increase in the Engineering News Record Construction Cost Index for the Los Angeles
Area (the “ENRLA”), as of February of each year. The City has not increased the sewer service
charges since FY 2017/18.

Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC), Chapter 13.14 and the California Health and Safety Code,
Article 4 of Chapter 6 of Part 3 of Division 5, Section 5470, affirms that City Council is authorized
to levy an annual sewer service charge and to have such charge collected on the property tax
roll.

As required by the California Health and Safety Code, each year that the City levies and collects
charges on the tax roll, the City must prepare a report that contains a description of each parcel
of real property to which the charge is applicable and the amount of the charge for each parcel
and must hold a public hearing. The report is available for public inspection in City Clerk’s Office
or viewed online at the City’s webpage. As provided in the report, the proposed charge for each
parcel is the amount authorized by NMC Chapter 13.14.020, Section E.

  ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023/24

  WHEREAS, the City Manager did heretofore submit to City Council an estimate of
the expenses and revenues of the City for a Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year 2023/24;
and

  WHEREAS, on May 11, 2023, said budget was presented to the Finance Ad Hoc
Committee; and

  WHEREAS, copies of said budget were prepared and on May 19, 2023, distributed
to the members of City Council; and

  WHEREAS, on May 19, 2023, copy of said budget was made available for public
inspection in the Office of the City Clerk and the City’s website; and

  WHEREAS, on May 30, 2023, the City Council held a Special meeting to discuss
the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year 2023/24; and

  WHEREAS, City Council set June 20, 2023, at the hour of 6:00 p.m., as the time
and place for holding a public hearing for the Fiscal Year 2023/24 Budget; and

  WHEREAS, the City, pursuant to Federal Regulations 24 CFR Part 570.301, as
amended, has obtained citizen comments on proposed projects which will be undertaken
using HCDA funds; and

  WHEREAS, after duly given and published as required by law, City Council did
hold such public hearing at said time and place upon said budget; and

  WHEREAS, all persons desiring to be heard by City Council at said public hearing
on the proposed budget were heard; and

  WHEREAS, City Council after due consideration has determined that said budget
should be approved.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The Operations and Capital Project Budgets for the period beginning
July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024 are adopted and the expenditures as indicated in
the budget and amended by City Council to consider same, are hereby appropriated out
of the public funds and the expenditures authorized to all departments, offices and
agencies for the respective objectives and purposes therein named, subject to the
 authority hereby granted to the City Manager to transfer appropriations from account to
account as necessary to assure adequate and proper standards of service and to achieve
the intent of City Council in providing municipal services for the identified period.

  Section 2. City Council gives approval for periodic reviews to be brought back
to City Council during the fiscal period to manage future unexpected changes in funding
sources and possible cost increases.

  Section 3. The Mayor, or presiding officer, is hereby authorized to affix her
signature to this Resolution signifying its adoption by the City Council of the City of
Norwalk and the City Clerk, or her duly appointed assistant, is directed to attest thereto.

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 20th day of June 2023.
